_schema.description: Human- or agent-reviewed theory threads. Similarity alone must not create milestones or links.

thread-hamptons-retreat-characterization.title: How the Hamptons retreat was characterized
thread-hamptons-retreat-characterization.summary: Tracks competing on-channel descriptions of the August 2025 Hamptons retreat: first as an intervention over Israel, then as a debate workshop, and later as a retreat convened by Charlie Kirk.

milestones.proposition: Owens first described the retreat in this corpus as a staged intervention organized because Kirk's views on Israel were unacceptable to participants.
milestones.review_note: The transcript directly supports that Owens made this characterization and attributed it to what she had been told. This milestone records the on-channel assertion, not independent proof that the retreat was an intervention.

milestones.proposition: Owens introduced Xavier DeRusso's account: Kirk spoke of moral blackmail, while DeRusso framed the gathering as a workshop or debate-club setting.
milestones.review_note: The surrounding transcript distinguishes Owens's summary from the DeRusso clip. This refines the earlier account by preserving pressure-related language while changing the described format of the meeting.

milestones.proposition: Seth Dillon disputed the intervention framing and said Kirk personally convened and led the retreat, while confirming a heated debate about Israel occurred.
milestones.review_note: The clip directly records Dillon rejecting the intervention description and offering a competing participant account. It contradicts the staging claim while corroborating that Israel was debated.

links.review_note: The later account adds a workshop framing without dropping the moral-pressure element.
Dillon explicitly says the retreat was not the intervention described in the earlier account.
